notes.note: Firefox's Local Network Access protections now extends to WebSocket connections. Websites that try to open a WebSocket to a device on your local network will now ask for your permission first.

In Smart Window, Firefox can now organize your open tabs
into groups for you by suggesting groupings of related tabs and naming each
one.

[Address autofill][1] has been enabled for users in all locales.


  [1]: https://support.mozilla.org/kb/automatically-fill-your-address-web-forms

You can now backup your profile locally on macOS devices and restore that profile between windows, macOS and linux. ([Learn more][1])


  [1]: https://support.mozilla.org/kb/firefox-backup
Exceptions for sites that have their cookies & site data cleared on shutdown can now be set without exempting the site from tracking protection and other cookie restrictions.
The full-page Translations feature now translates `<iframe>` content.
The full-page Translations feature now runs language identification on all page loads, resulting in an improved experience for offering translations to users.
Firefox now gives Windows users the ability to change their default browser icon in Settings (except for MSIX installs). Support for MSIX installs, macOS and Linux is coming soon.

The address bar now includes a "Manage AI" [quick action][1] that opens the AI section of Settings.


  [1]: https://support.mozilla.org/kb/quick-actions-firefox-search-bar
Performing a hard reload on a page (holding Shift while clicking the Refresh button) now also clears and updates its cached favicons.
Video seeking is now significantly faster on macOS, making scrubbing and jumping to a point in a video much more responsive.
Text selected in PDFs is now highlighted clearly like in normal web pages. The selection color also follows OS settings like high-contrast mode.

Firefox View is moving out of the toolbar by default for new profiles and profiles where it hasn’t been used recently. You can still open it from *List all tabs > View all tabs*, or add it back from the *Customize toolbar* menu.
Added a time picker user interface to `<input type="time">` and `<input type="datetime-local">,` making selecting a time more accessible and intuitive.

Firefox now supports the `text-box-trim` and `text-box-edge` CSS properties, and the associated `text-box` shorthand. These properties allow you to control the leading space above and below text, enabling simpler and consistent vertical spacing and alignment.

Firefox now supports the [sibling-index()][1] and [sibling-count()][2] CSS functions. These functions allow an element to be styled with calculations that use its index among its siblings and its total count of siblings (including itself), respectively.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/sibling-index
  [2]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/sibling-count

Added support for the [No-Vary-Search][1] HTTP response header for the HTTP disk cache. Servers can now declare which URL query parameters are irrelevant to the response, allowing Firefox to reuse cached resources across parameter variations and improving cache hit rates.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/No-Vary-Search

Firefox now supports new [Iterator.prototype.chunks][1] and Iterator.prototype.windows methods that allow consuming an iterator as either overlapping or non-overlapping subsequences of configurable size.


  [1]: https://github.com/tc39/proposal-iterator-chunking

Firefox now supports [Iterator.prototype.includes()][1], allowing developers to check whether an iterator contains a given value without first converting it to an array.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Iterator/includes

Firefox now supports the [Iterator.prototype.join][1] method that allows joining an iterator into a string, similar to Array.prototype.join.


  [1]: https://github.com/tc39/proposal-iterator-join
The JSON Viewer now shows a breadcrumb path at the bottom for the selected entry.

You can find information about policy updates and enterprise-specific bug fixes in the [Firefox for Enterprise 154 Release Notes][1].


  [1]: https://support.mozilla.org/kb/firefox-enterprise-154-release-notes
Fixed an issue on macOS where closing a browser window could leave behind an invisible window that continued to capture mouse clicks over the area where it used to be.
If the Windows taskbar is set to auto-hide, Firefox will no longer require minimizing/maximizing after launch to allow the Windows taskbar to show.
When using Vertical Tabs in full screen mode, the sidebar is now hidden along with the toolbars, and reappears when moving the cursor to the edge of the screen.
The display of PDF documents in the print-preview are now scaled correctly when using “Fit to Page Width” option.

Various [security fixes][1].


  [1]: https://www.mozilla.org/security/advisories/mfsa2026

With the release of Firefox 154, we are pleased to welcome the developers who contributed their first code change to Firefox in this release, 32 of whom were brand new volunteers! system_requirements:
## Windows

### Operating Systems (32-bit and 64-bit)
 - Windows 10 or later

### Recommended Hardware
-  1 gigahertz (GHz) or faster compatible processor or System on a Chip (SoC)
-  1GB of RAM / 2GB of RAM for the 64-bit version
-  500MB of hard drive space

---

## Mac

### Operating Systems
- macOS 10.15 or later 

### Recommended Hardware
- Macintosh computer with an Intel x86 or Apple silicon processor
- 512 MB of RAM
- 200 MB hard drive space

---

## GNU/Linux

### Software Requirements

*Please note that GNU/Linux distributors may provide packages for your distribution which have different requirements.*


- Firefox will not run at all without the following libraries or packages:
    - glibc 2.17 or higher (glibc 2.28 or higher on arm64)
    - GTK+ 3.14 or higher
    - libglib 2.42 or higher
    - libstdc++ 4.8.1 or higher (libstdc++ 6.0 or higher on arm64)
    - X.Org 1.0 or higher (1.7 or higher is recommended)
- For optimal functionality, we recommend the following libraries or packages:
    - DBus 1.0 or higher
    - NetworkManager 0.7 or higher
    - PulseAudio
